public_comment.topic: Unintended consequences of not fully funding the schools: staff wearing too many hats, larger high school class sections, and deteriorating building cleanliness/maintenance.
Updates on grassroots override campaign efforts: a Zoom strategy meeting, PTO endorsement, planned social media posts, and support for the blue-ribbon idea.

votes.motion: Motion to approve the regular session minutes of February 7th
Motion to move the second public comment period to right now
Motion to approve the curriculum change to the Ed Gems math curriculum for grades 6 through 8
Motion to accept the donated comfort blankets from the United Parish Church
Motion to go into executive session at 8:57 p.m. and adjourn following

budget_items.what_was_said: The food service department will prepare and sell bag lunches to town meeting attendees, covering its own cost rather than being funded by the school budget.

budget_items.topic: ESSER/ARPA funds and the override, compared to a neighboring town
budget_items.what_was_said: A member pushed back on the public assumption that the override is entirely about ESSER funds ending, citing a newspaper editorial and noting a neighboring town's override wasn't all ESSER-funded either.
The finance committee liaison reported the town meeting warrant article number and dollar figure for the school override that voters will see.

budget_items.topic: Middle school math curriculum purchase funding
budget_items.what_was_said: The new math curriculum and a multi-year digital subscription will be funded mainly through grant money, intended to keep the cost off next year's local operating budget.
Funding draws from an evidence-based-practices grant that also pays for a co-teacher and math specialist, plus smaller portions from a special education grant and the curriculum adoption budget line.
Remaining cultural council funds originally meant for a high school artist-in-residence program will instead be spread across all schools after the program's organizer resigned.
Funding was secured for a design and assessment process for Turkey Hill Elementary on the capital plan up for town meeting approval, expected to kick off a larger future process.

The superintendent described ongoing difficulty pulling budget and financial reports from the town's newly upgraded MUNIS platform without a finance director in place, hampering both the school committee and town hall.

decisions.decision: Edits to the override communication statement will route through the superintendent, who compiles member feedback and sends it to the chair to finalize, avoiding a group email chain under the open meeting law.
The chair and another member will prepare override presentation slides for a 'dry run' at the May 1st meeting ahead of town meeting.
The chair will finalize and release the override communication statement within about a week, before town meeting.
The committee will let parents (not the school committee itself) lead a blue-ribbon display as a no-cost show of support for the override.
The core-values/strategic-plan facilitation discussion is postponed to September or October given the current budget workload.
The superintendent will try to arrange a special meeting or virtual attendance by a physician connected to MIAA to answer questions on athletic head-injury protocol.
Remaining artist-in-residence funds will be spread across all schools, with the director of teaching and learning coordinating artist selection.
Town meeting attendees will be allowed to eat bag lunches in the auditorium, with a formal vote expected May 1st.
The superintendent will present an overview of school funding sources and the athletic budget report at the next meeting, alongside the override presentation.

minutes.headline: Committee finalized how it will communicate the school override to voters ahead of the May 4 town meeting.
minutes.summary: The meeting centered on finalizing a public communication plan for the school budget override before town meeting: a statement drafted by the chair, a "dry run" presentation planned for the next meeting, and grassroots support ideas like blue ribbons, alongside frank internal debate over whether the committee communicates well with the public. The committee also voted to adopt a new middle school math curriculum funded largely by grants, accepted a donation of comfort blankets, reviewed its annual goals (crediting itself on transparency but faulting its own public communication), and heard continuing frustration over the town's inability to produce timely financial reports without a finance director.

what_happened.line: The chair will finalize and release a public statement on the school override before the May 4 town meeting.
The committee voted to adopt a new middle school math curriculum, funded mainly through grants rather than the operating budget.
The committee voted to accept a donation of comfort blankets from a local church group.
The superintendent said the school department still cannot reliably pull financial reports from the town's MUNIS system without a finance director in place.

why_it_matters: The override statement and a planned dry-run presentation shape what residents hear before voting on the school budget at town meeting.
Funding the new math curriculum through grants is meant to keep that cost off next year's school operating budget rather than being cost-free permanently.
Difficulty producing timely financial reports touches how residents and the committee itself can check budget figures ahead of votes.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the meeting's two substantive School Committee votes (Ed Gems curriculum, blanket donation) and on most non-financial decisions, but the official minutes omit several votes and figures our transcript captured (a motion to move public comment, the override dollar amount, the ESSER/ARPA comparison) while we omit some the official minutes have (the roll-call minutes vote, the Finance Committee's override recommendation, the warrant total). The one item a reader should check first is the chair's identity: our minutes list "Kate" as chair, but the official minutes show Carol Archambault as Chair and Dr. Kate Burnham as the Superintendent — a role mix-up, not just a misheard name.
